quarterly_data.quarter: Munters press release: Significant order growth as operational improvements (10-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 interim report (release): order intake up 70%, driven by Data Center Technologies (DCT) and AirTech; net sales up 18%, driven by all business areas, particularly AirTech; the adjusted EBITA margin declined as DCT's margin fell on changed product mix, component shortages and ramp-up inefficiencies, while AirTech's adjusted EBITA margin rose by close to 6 p.p. (approx. 2.5 p.p. from a non-recurring order cancellation fee) and its profit more than doubled; operating cash flow was negative mainly on DCT inventory build-up; OWC/net sales 4.2%; leverage 3.4x (3.2x in Q2 2026); EPS SEK 1.16 (1.05). The outlook for 2026 is unchanged, and the process to explore a potential divestment of FoodTech is progressing according to plan.
quarterly_data.figure: order intake +70%; net sales +18%; leverage 3.4x; EPS SEK 1.16

quarterly_data.quarter: Munters press release: Significant order growth as operational improvements (10-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DCT (CEO Stefan Aspman, Q3 2026 release): DCT order intake more than doubled year on year, outpacing an exceptionally strong underlying data center market, with the US the main stronghold, increasing traction in EMEA and early progress in Asia; DCT net sales rose 15% year on year and around 30% sequentially as manufacturing scales after the Daleville, Virginia campus expansion, broadly in line with the plan to reach significantly higher production volumes towards the end of the year, though component availability affected the pace of the ramp-up. Supply-chain constraints and tariff effects still weighed on profitability; the supply-chain situation has partly improved, but constraints remain industry-wide.
quarterly_data.figure: DCT net sales +15% year on year, around 30% sequentially
